conclusion.first_identity: query κ x = (κ − 1) • query 2 x − (κ − 2) • x.

constant_dependencies.diagonal_formula: Each entry is (η + 1)/2 + (η − 1)/2 · cos(θ(i)); the same η is used in both affine terms.
constant_dependencies.dimension_and_matrix_dependence: d fixes all index and vector spaces; O fixes the common orthogonal conjugation. There are no unspecified constants or probability-law dependencies.

constant_dependencies.identity_coefficients: The first identity uses κ − 1 and κ − 2. The second uses the reciprocal of κ − 1 and the same κ − 2.
constant_dependencies.reciprocal_meaning: At zero the approved convention gives reciprocal zero; under κ ≥ 2 the displayed reciprocal is the usual inverse.
constant_dependencies.π_and_cos: Real.pi and Real.cos are the ordinary real constant π and cosine function.

reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every natural number d with d ≥ 2, every real number κ with κ ≥ 2, and every real orthogonal d × d matrix O (with either determinant sign), index coordinates by i ∈ Fin d, that is, integers i = 0, …, d − 1. Define
θᵢ = (i + 1/2)π/d.
For each real parameter η, define
A(η) = O diagᵢ((η + 1)/2 + ((η − 1)/2) cos θᵢ) Oᵀ,
and define Qη : ℝᵈ → ℝᵈ by Qη(x) = A(η)x, using ordinary matrix-vector multiplication and the usual Euclidean coordinate identification.
Then every x ∈ ℝᵈ satisfies both vector identities
Qκ(x) = (κ − 1) Q₂(x) − (κ − 2)x,
and
Q₂(x) = (κ − 1)⁻¹ (Qκ(x) + (κ − 2)x).
Here scalar-vector products and vector sums and differences have their usual real meanings. The same d, κ, O, and x occur in both identities. Since κ ≥ 2, κ − 1 is nonzero and its displayed reciprocal is the usual real inverse. No probability law on O is specified.

scopes.A: Depends on the fixed O and θ (hence d) and is evaluated at its own real argument η.
scopes.conjunction: Uses the same d, κ, O, θ, A, query, and universally chosen x in both conjuncts.
scopes.matrix_order: O · diagonal · Oᵀ; no factor is permuted.
scopes.parentheses: The reciprocal (κ − 1)⁻¹ scales the entire vector sum query κ x + (κ − 2) • x in the second identity.
scopes.query: Uses that same A and its arguments η and x; coordinate conversions preserve entries.
scopes.θ: Depends only on d and its coordinate i, with π fixed.
